clue.text: Nick, getting out of bed, is distressed

parts.note: to nick is to make a small cut
someone rising from bed is up

explanation.surface: Someone called Nick is upset as he gets out of bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a man's name; it is the verb meaning to cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cut up is an informal idiom for being deeply upset.

clue.text: Picture only half seen with right viewfinder?

parts.note: a painting on canvas

indicators.note: just the first half of the word is kept

explanation.surface: A picture, half seen, is fixed with the right viewfinder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'viewfinder' is not part of a camera but someone who finds out people's views.
explanation.definitionFit: A canvasser goes door to door finding out people's opinions, so is a finder of views.

clue.text: Contemptible creature picked up by the ears may be drawn

indicators.note: heard, so a word of like sound is meant

parts.note: a toad is a loathsome person or creature

explanation.surface: A vile creature caught by its ears may be pulled along.
explanation.definitionFit: Something towed is pulled along behind a vehicle, just as a cart is drawn.

clue.text: Characteristic buildings

definitions.meaning: real estate, houses and land owned

explanation.definitionFit: The word means an attribute of something and also real estate owned.

clue.text: Poem written by Kipling during important match

indicators.note: one piece sits within the time of the other, so it goes inside

parts.note: a seminal work is highly important and influential
Rudyard Kipling wrote the famous poem If

explanation.surface: A Kipling poem is read out at a big sporting fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: A semifinal is the match played to decide who reaches a final.

clue.text: Alcoholic drink for Pete's follower?

definitions.meaning: the word after for Pete's in the exclamation

explanation.definitionFit: Sake is Japanese rice wine, and also follows for Pete's in the exasperated exclamation.

clue.text: Daisy is small child entertaining contender

indicators.note: the outer word hosts the inner one

parts.note: a mite is a little child
an arguer contends a point

explanation.surface: Daisy is a toddler playing host to a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daisy' looks like a girl's name; it is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The marguerite is the ox-eye daisy, a common white-petalled flower.

clue.text: Knowing about a British bulldog, originally lacking vitality

indicators.note: the outer word goes round the other letters

parts.note: fly is British slang for sharp and knowing

indicators.note: just the opening letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A British bulldog, once fit, now lacks energy.
explanation.walkthrough: FLY is British slang for shrewd or knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Flabby means slack and weak, without firmness or vigour.

clue.text: Brief report of Welsh fans rioting

indicators.note: unruly letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A short bulletin on Welsh supporters causing trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsflash is a short urgent item of news that interrupts broadcasting.

clue.text: Row over name for material

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: a line is a row

explanation.surface: A dispute about a name for a fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a quarrel; it is a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Linen is a fabric woven from flax.

clue.text: Queens resident, possibly ignoring king, was aware of delivery

indicators.note: leaving out the letter for king from the word before

parts.note: to have been aware is to have known
K is the chess abbreviation for king
a yorker is a cricket ball pitched at the batter's feet

explanation.surface: A Queens local, never minding the monarch, knew about a delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: A YORKER is a cricket delivery bowled to land right at the batter's feet. 'Queens' is the New York borough, not royalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Queens is one of the boroughs of New York City, so its residents are an example of its citizens.

clue.text: A glider for an Egyptian city

parts.note: a swan glides gracefully across water

explanation.surface: A glider is swapped for travel to a city in Egypt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'glider' suggests an aircraft; it is a swan gliding on water.
explanation.definitionFit: Aswan is a city on the Nile in southern Egypt, famous for its dam.

clue.text: Patron saint has doctor brought in again

indicators.note: one piece is taken inside the other

parts.note: to do something anew is to do it again

explanation.surface: A saint's shrine calls in its physician once more.
explanation.definitionFit: St Andrew is the patron saint of Scotland.

clue.text: Dry back of an engine

indicators.note: the word for dry is read from the back

parts.note: brut describes very dry champagne

explanation.surface: The rear of an engine is dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses BRUT, a term for very dry champagne, to give TURB.
explanation.definitionFit: A turbofan is a jet engine type used on most airliners.

clue.text: Composer doesn't finish port that's passed

indicators.note: the last letter of the composer's name is dropped

parts.note: Handel was a German-born British baroque composer
Dover is the English Channel port

explanation.surface: A composer leaves a port unfinished and moves on.
explanation.definitionFit: Something handed over has been passed from one person to another.

clue.text: To be pedantic, it is Ralph's shot

indicators.note: shot in the sense of ruined or broken up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken with its final S as letters

explanation.surface: Someone fussy says a shot was Ralph's.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the S of 'Ralph's' counts as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To split hairs is an idiom for quibbling over tiny distinctions.

clue.text: Fancy stories Tory leader made most plausible

parts.note: to fancy is to like
lies are invented stories

indicators.note: the first letter leads the word

explanation.surface: Imagined tales from a Tory leader seemed most believable.
explanation.definitionFit: The likeliest option is the one most probable or credible.

clue.text: Story, a real laugh going round

indicators.note: turning round makes the phrase read backwards

parts.note: something hilarious is informally a gas

explanation.surface: A tale that is great fun gets passed around.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a long narrative, originally an Icelandic tale of heroes.

clue.text: Can I turn in fruit machine?

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: an apple is a fruit

indicators.note: the letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: May I have a go on the fruit machine?
explanation.walkthrough: 'fruit machine' is the British name for a slot machine; here it splits apart.
explanation.definitionFit: An appliance is a device or machine for a household task.

clue.text: Briars to entangle tree surgeon

indicators.note: tangled letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Thorny briars ensnare a tree surgeon.
explanation.definitionFit: An arborist cares for and prunes trees professionally.

clue.text: Tool set at a sloping angle

definitions.meaning: a garden implement with tines on a long handle
a stage or mast may be inclined like this

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a garden implement and also means to incline, as a raked stage.

clue.text: Organ's head office reorganised Irish depot

indicators.note: the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A newspaper's top post moves to a reorganised Irish depot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' is a newspaper or journal, not the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The post of editor is the head office at a newspaper or periodical.

clue.text: Top marks in succession for goddess?

parts.note: A is the top grade
then means next in order
a second top grade

explanation.surface: Getting the best grades one after another is divine.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful reading of A THEN A.
explanation.definitionFit: Athena is the Greek goddess of wisdom.

clue.text: Bother with source of water for flush

parts.note: a well is a source of water
a to-do is a fuss or bother

explanation.surface: Trouble with the water supply for a toilet's flush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flush' looks like the toilet; it means having plenty of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Being flush with money is an idiom for being wealthy or comfortably off.

clue.text: Carried on in paid employment

definitions.meaning: conducted, as a war or campaign

explanation.definitionFit: The word means conducted, as a war is, and also describes earning a regular wage.

clue.text: Dog, black one, eating small pieces of pasta

indicators.note: the outer letters take in the pasta

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black on pencils
I is the Roman numeral for one
orzo is rice-shaped pasta

explanation.surface: A black dog eats some small bits of pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: The borzoi is a Russian wolfhound breed.

clue.text: Country, formerly unknown, made known for the most part

parts.note: Z is a mathematical unknown

indicators.note: the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to air views is to make them known

explanation.surface: A country once unknown has largely been made public.
explanation.definitionFit: Zaire was the name of the Democratic Republic of the Congo from 1971 to 1997.

clue.text: Baffling problem in vineyard close to Bordeaux

parts.note: a cru is a classified French vineyard

indicators.note: the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: A puzzle at a vineyard near Bordeaux.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' looks like 'near'; it means the end of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: The crux is the central or most difficult point of a problem.

clue.text: Joy with bishop in the land of the living?

indicators.note: the letter for bishop goes inside the word for joy

parts.note: glee is happiness
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: Happiness with a bishop in the land of the living.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'living' is a church benefice; this field was land that supported the vicar holding it.
explanation.definitionFit: A glebe is a piece of land attached to a parish church to support the incumbent's benefice.

clue.text: Maid Marian, half-cut, coming from Richmond perhaps

parts.note: a maid in the old sense is a virgin

indicators.note: the word loses half its letters

explanation.surface: Maid Marian, rather tipsy, is from Richmond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' means drunk in British slang; here it removes MAR. Richmond is the capital of Virginia.
explanation.definitionFit: Richmond is the state capital of Virginia, so someone from there is an example of a native.

clue.text: Time to stop sadistic woman dropping in for type of printer

indicators.note: the time letter plugs a gap in the other word
dropping in the sense of letting go, so the two letters of the word in fall out

parts.note: a dominatrix inflicts pain for pleasure

explanation.surface: A dominatrix stops in, buying a printer.
explanation.walkthrough: DOMINATRIX loses IN to become DOMATRIX, then T stops the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A dot-matrix printer forms characters from patterns of tiny dots.

clue.text: On the spot it may be said to be comforting

definitions.text: it may be said to be comforting
definitions.meaning: the soothing words used to calm someone upset

explanation.definitionFit: The word means in that place and, doubled, is a soothing phrase of consolation.
